clue.text: Expression of regret that the game was held in a gym, no member present

indicators.note: being held in something means sitting inside it, so the game goes within the other letters
M is a standard abbreviation for member; with none present it is struck from the word gym

parts.note: the clue word itself, a gymnasium
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: Someone apologises because a match was staged in a gym with no players turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no member present' removes M (member) from GYM, leaving GY; 'was held in' puts POLO between A and GY.
explanation.definitionFit: An apology is a formal statement saying sorry, which is an expression of regret.

clue.text: Kidnaps French nobleman with wild stab outside

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters sit on either side of the nobleman
wild means the letters of stab are rearranged

parts.note: duc is the French word for duke

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat is seized and stabbed by a frenzied attacker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges STAB, split as AB and TS, and 'outside' puts it around DUC.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct is to carry someone off by force, to seize and hold them.

clue.text: Try too hard to get above the stretch of the river

parts.note: over means above
a reach is a straight stretch of a river between bends

explanation.surface: A rower strains to get past a long section of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreach is to overextend oneself by aiming beyond one's ability.

clue.text: Gold lace, some for rising stars

indicators.note: some says only part of the words is taken, here a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Golden trim is put aside for the latest celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'fOR RISing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is an old name for lace or braid of gold or silver thread.

clue.text: Youth leader realigns unsettled horses

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
unsettled means the letters of realigns are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A youth leader rearranges a team of nervous horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes Y from 'Youth'; 'unsettled' rearranges REALIGNS into EARLINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is an animal in its second year, used especially of a young racehorse.

clue.text: Lay clause out before first reading

indicators.note: before places the rearranged clause ahead of the following piece
out signals that the letters of clause are put out of order
first takes just the opening letter of the word reading

explanation.surface: A legal clause is set aside before the first reading of a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CLAUSE into SECULA; 'first' takes R from 'reading'. 'Lay' is the adjective meaning not of the clergy, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay people are not clergy, so lay matters are worldly rather than religious, which is the sense of non-religious.

clue.text: Moults in outbuildings

explanation.surface: An animal loses its coat inside farm buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to cast off skin or hair, and a shed is a simple hut or store.

clue.text: Snug place for young animal near the pit

parts.note: a cub is the young of a fox, bear or lion
by means near or beside
a hole is a pit dug in the ground

explanation.surface: A cosy den for a fox cub close to a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small enclosed cosy space, like a cupboard or nook.

clue.text: Can the French come first in language?

indicators.note: come first says the French article is placed ahead of the can

parts.note: la is the French for the (feminine)
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Is it a can that comes first in language?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb opening the question, but it is the noun TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is the classical tongue of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Withstands sister's reforms

indicators.note: reforms means forms again, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A sister fights off reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges SISTERS; here the 's adds an S to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to stand firm against something, to oppose it.

clue.text: Gloomy physician needs a listener

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, a physician
an ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A depressed doctor needs someone to listen to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning dismal and cheerless.

clue.text: Creates confusion around Jack's return which is irritating

indicators.note: around tells us the rearranged letters wrap about the other piece
confusion means the letters of creates are jumbled
return means the sailor's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the standard abbreviation for one

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble about Jack coming back, which is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' rearranges CREATES into ACERTES; 'return' turns AB (able seaman, Jack) into BA, and 'around' puts that inside to give ACER-BA-TES.
explanation.definitionFit: To acerbate is to embitter or exasperate, so something that acerbates is annoying people.

clue.text: Shed tears round hospital-young Sarah is an intermediate case

indicators.note: round says the weeping word goes round the hospital letter

parts.note: to shed tears is to cry
H is the abbreviation for hospital on signs and maps
Sal is a pet form of the name Sarah

explanation.surface: Little Sarah weeps around the hospital as a patient between stages.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'case' is a casing: the hard shell a caterpillar forms between larva and adult.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupa's protective shell is the stage between caterpillar and butterfly, so it is a casing at the in-between stage.

clue.text: But not all Americans are such jerks!

definitions.text: But not all Americans are such

explanation.surface: A remark that not every American is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Yanks is slang for Americans, and to yank is to pull sharply; the surface uses 'jerks' as insulting people, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee is a nickname for people from the United States (true of only some Americans), and a sharp pull is a tug or jerk.

clue.text: Girl without a penny for fashion

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the girl's word goes around the rest

parts.note: she stands for any girl or woman
P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: A girl goes without a single penny to spend on clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: SHE goes round A and P. 'fashion' is the verb, to form or mould.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion something is to form or mould it, the same as giving it a form.

clue.text: Are about to throw out a thousand of the grub species

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved around into another order

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone is about to discard a thousand larvae.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ARE and THROW to give EARTHWOR, and M (a thousand) finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing soil worm, the sort of crawling creature loosely called a grub.

clue.text: Drugs that put oxygen into northern oceans

indicators.note: into says the oxygen letter is put inside the rest

parts.note: the Arctic seas, used as a plural noun for the polar oceans
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Narcotics that pollute the northern oceans with oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: O (oxygen) goes inside N (northern) + ARCTICS, the Arctic waters made plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics are drugs that dull the senses, used in the sense of illegal substances.

clue.text: Tricks about money, with the schilling showing result of lack of use

indicators.note: about says the tricks go around the money

parts.note: ruses are tricks
tin is old slang for money
S is the abbreviation for the schilling, the old Austrian currency

explanation.surface: Money tricks with an Austrian coin reveal how out of practice someone is.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN, old slang for money, goes inside RUSES, followed by S for the schilling, Austria's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustiness is the stiffness or loss of skill that comes from being out of practice.

clue.text: Slip maybe to have provided Ulster's comeback with church dignitary

indicators.note: comeback signals that the preceding words together are read backwards

parts.note: if means provided that
NI, Northern Ireland, is often called Ulster
an elder is an official of a Presbyterian church

explanation.surface: A church elder returns from Ulster after a slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' turns IF + NI into INFI. In cricket, slip is a fielding position close to the batter, part of the infield.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fielder stationed close in, as a slip fielder is, belongs to the infield.

clue.text: I'm so sharp over pithy sayings

indicators.note: over, as in knocked over, signals that the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being so sharp that they are full of witty one-liners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' rearranges the letters of I'M SO SHARP.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphorisms are short memorable statements of a truth, like maxims.

clue.text: After a very quiet start, moving in to select candidates

indicators.note: start says those letters begin the answer, ahead of the rest

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet

indicators.note: moving signals that the letters of in to change places

explanation.surface: After a hushed opening, the committee moves in to choose the candidates.
explanation.walkthrough: A and PP (very quiet) start it; 'moving' rearranges IN TO into OINT.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint is to choose someone for an office or job.

clue.text: Impish female was trapped by receding river

indicators.note: being trapped by something means being held inside it
receding means moving back, so the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: A mischievous woman was caught by a river as it went down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receding' turns NILE into ELIN, and 'was trapped by' puts F (female) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are mischievous little sprites, so elfin means puckish, like an imp.

clue.text: Having been sent off, went ahead to get settled

indicators.note: off, as in gone off, says the letters of sent are disordered

parts.note: led means went in front

explanation.surface: A footballer sent off then walked ahead to sit down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SENT into NEST; LED (went ahead) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to settle snugly and comfortably into a place.

clue.text: Like asphalt playing field

explanation.surface: A sports ground surfaced with tarmac.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch is a black tarry substance like bitumen, and in Britain a pitch is the ground on which football or cricket is played.

clue.text: Mobile home for brave person

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, and the portable home is the cone-shaped tent of the Plains peoples

explanation.surface: A caravan for someone courageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' looks like an adjective for a bold person, but it is the noun for a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A conical tent of skins that Native Americans carried from camp to camp.

clue.text: Inability to see why bishop left sin's end out

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bishop in chess notation

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the words before it are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why a bishop omitted the end of a sinful story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SINS END into INDNESS, after B (bishop) and L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Blindness is lack of sight, the condition of being sightless.

clue.text: William catches river fish

indicators.note: catches means holds, so the river letter goes inside the name

parts.note: Bill is a short form of William

explanation.surface: William catches a fish in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Brill is a flatfish related to the turbot.

clue.text: Leave forces behind on march to Birkenhead

indicators.note: behind places the letter after the march

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
the head of Birken, its first letter, is B

explanation.surface: A soldier leaves the army after a march to the port of Birkenhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Birkenhead is a town on Merseyside; its 'head', the first letter, is B, coming behind DEMO.
explanation.definitionFit: To demob is to discharge someone from the armed services.

clue.text: Tickle the ivories with politician breaking in to give extempore performance

indicators.note: breaking in means forcing a way inside, so the politician goes into the other letters
to tickle is to stir or play with lightly, signalling the letters of ivories are rearranged

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a British politician

explanation.surface: A pianist plays, joined by a politician who barges in, making it all up on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tickle the ivories' means play the piano and fits the scene; here 'Tickle' rearranges IVORIES to IROVISE, and 'breaking in' puts MP inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to make something up without preparation, ad lib.

clue.text: Exemplary poem line after fifth attempt

indicators.note: after puts the poem and line behind the letter taken from attempt
fifth takes the letter in fifth place in the word attempt

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A model poem written only after five tries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifth' picks the fifth letter of 'attempt', M; ODE and L come 'after' it. The surface reads 'fifth attempt' as a fifth try.
explanation.definitionFit: A model pupil or model citizen is an ideal one, exemplary as an adjective.

clue.text: The right to hit back at current activity

indicators.note: back means the word for hit is read in reverse

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit

explanation.surface: A person claims the right to retaliate over what is happening now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LAM (to beat) into MAL. 'current' is a flow of air, not the present.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermal is a rising column of warm air, used by gliders and birds to gain height.

clue.text: Became more serious when society awarded honour to revolutionary

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary grew solemn when a society gave them a royal honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is an award in the British honours system.
explanation.definitionFit: To sober is to make or grow calm and earnest, losing levity.
